document_name: FSS (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, FSDU, FSMP, Functional Food & Novel Food) Regulations 2022
summary_text: Gazette Notification S.O. 4027(E) — India's first comprehensive regulatory framework for health supplements and nutraceuticals. Replaces the 2016 draft framework. Mandates product type declaration, FSSAI license display, 'NOT FOR MEDICINAL USE' statement, %RDA declaration per ICMR-NIN 2020 values, prohibited disease claims, and a positive ingredient list with upper safe limits. Companies given 12-month transition period to reformulate labels.
diff_text:
Key provisions introduced:

Schedule I — Permitted ingredients with maximum limits
Schedule II — Prohibited ingredients and claims
Schedule III — Labelling requirements
  - Clause 3.1: Product type declaration mandatory on front of pack
  - Clause 3.2: FSSAI 14-digit license number in specified format
  - Clause 3.3: 'NOT FOR MEDICINAL USE' in Arial/Helvetica min 2mm
  - Clause 3.5: Nutritional information per serving + per 100g
  - Clause 3.6: %RDA declaration using ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA values
  - Clause 3.8: Expiry date in Month/Year format mandatory
  - Clause 3.9: Country of origin mandatory
Schedule IV — Permitted health claims (structure/function only)

document_name: FSSAI Order: Prohibition of 14 Ingredients in Health Supplements — F.No.Stds/HS/Nutra/2022
summary_text: Immediate ban on 14 ingredients previously used in weight management and sports nutrition products. Companies must withdraw products containing these ingredients within 90 days. No transition period — products already in market must be recalled. Action taken following adverse event reports and EFSA safety review.
diff_text:
Ingredients banned with immediate effect:

1. Raspberry Ketone (4-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-2-butanone)
   Reason: Insufficient safety data; potential thyroid interference

2. Saw Palmetto (Serenoa repens extract)
   Reason: Hormonal activity; contraindicated without medical supervision

3. Guarana (Paullinia cupana seed extract)
   Reason: Uncontrolled caffeine delivery; cardiovascular risk

4. Angelica sinensis (Dong Quai root extract)
   Reason: Coumarin content; drug interactions with anticoagulants

5. Panax notoginseng (Tienchi Ginseng)
   Reason: Blood clotting interference; inadequate safety data for OTC use

6. Chaga mushroom extract (Inonotus obliquus)
   Reason: Oxalate nephropathy risk; case reports of kidney stones

7. Chlorella Growth Factor (CGF)
   Reason: Inconsistent composition; inadequate safety substantiation

8. Tea Tree Oil (Melaleuca alternifolia) for internal use
   Reason: Toxic when ingested; CNS effects reported

9. Aristolochic acid-containing herbs
   Reason: Proven nephrotoxin and carcinogen

10. Ephedra (Ma Huang) all species
    Reason: Cardiovascular deaths reported; banned globally

11. Kava (Piper methysticum)
    Reason: Hepatotoxicity; liver failure cases documented

12. Pennyroyal (Mentha pulegium)
    Reason: Hepatotoxic; abortifacient effects

13. Colloidal Silver
    Reason: Argyria; no proven health benefit; heavy metal accumulation

14. Androstenedione
    Reason: Anabolic steroid precursor; banned in sports; hormonal risks

document_name: FSSAI Guidance Note: Mandatory FSSAI License Number Display on Nutraceutical Labels
summary_text: Clarification on display requirements for the 14-digit FSSAI license number. Must appear on the principal display panel with minimum font size 1.5mm, preceded by 'FSSAI Lic. No.' or 'FSSAI License No.' Barcode or QR representation not acceptable as substitute for printed license number.
diff_text:
Requirements clarified:
- Format: 'FSSAI Lic. No. XXXXXXXXXXXXXX' (14 digits)
- Location: Principal display panel (front of pack)
- Font: Minimum 1.5mm height, legible colour contrast
- NOT acceptable: QR code only, back-of-pack only
- Manufacturer's license required; importer/distributor license not sufficient for product manufactured domestically
- Imported products: FSSAI import approval number in same format

document_name: FSSAI Circular: Mandatory 'NOT FOR MEDICINAL USE' Statement — Health Supplements & Nutraceuticals
summary_text: All health supplements and nutraceuticals must carry 'NOT FOR MEDICINAL USE' on the principal display panel. Statement must be in English and the local language of sale. Minimum font size 2mm, all caps, in a box or visually distinct area. Statement must not be obscured by other design elements.
diff_text:
Placement requirements:
- Location: Principal display panel (front of pack), upper third preferred
- Font: ALL CAPITALS, minimum 2mm, Arial, Helvetica or similar sans-serif
- Language: English + regional language of primary market
- Visual: Enclosed in a ruled box OR printed in contrasting colour
- Must NOT be: Smaller than product name font, obscured by imagery

Non-compliance: Product liable to be treated as misbranded drug under Drugs & Cosmetics Act

document_name: FSSAI Notification: %RDA Declaration Using ICMR-NIN 2020 Reference Values
summary_text: Supersedes 2010 ICMR RDA values. All %RDA declarations on health supplement and nutraceutical labels must now be calculated against ICMR-NIN 2020 Dietary Reference Values. Updated values affect Vitamin D (600 IU → 800 IU), Vitamin B12, Folate, Zinc and several other micronutrients. Companies must recalculate and reprint labels within 60 days.
diff_text:
Key changes in reference values (selected):

Vitamin D: 600 IU/day → 800 IU/day (adult)
Vitamin B12: 2.2 mcg/day → 2.5 mcg/day
Folate: 400 mcg DFE/day → 450 mcg DFE/day
Zinc: 12 mg/day → 11 mg/day (men), 10 mg/day (women)
Iron: 17 mg/day → 15 mg/day (men)
Calcium: 600 mg/day → 800 mg/day
Magnesium: 340 mg/day → 360 mg/day
Vitamin C: 65 mg/day → 80 mg/day
Omega-3 (ALA): no previous value → 1.6 g/day (men), 1.1 g/day (women)

Source: ICMR-NIN Expert Group Report 2020 'Nutrient Requirements for Indians'

document_name: FSSAI Circular: Veg/Non-Veg Symbol Mandatory Placement — Front of Pack
summary_text: Reiterates and strengthens requirement for veg (green square with green circle) and non-veg (brown square with brown circle) symbols. Symbol must be on the principal display panel adjacent to product name. Minimum size 5mm × 5mm. Symbols must not be altered in colour or design. Products derived from marine sources (fish oil, krill oil) must display non-veg symbol.
diff_text:
Updated specifications:
- Green symbol: Pantone 361C (dark green square, dark green filled circle inside)
- Brown symbol: Pantone 7526C (brown square, brown filled circle inside)
- Minimum dimensions: 5mm × 5mm
- Location: Adjacent to or immediately below product name, front of pack
- NEW: Omega-3 from fish/krill sources — non-veg symbol mandatory even if product marketed as 'natural'
- NEW: Probiotic cultures of animal origin — non-veg symbol required
- Dual-source products (veg + non-veg ingredients): Non-veg symbol takes precedence

document_name: FSSAI Guidance: Allergen Declaration Requirements for Health Supplements
summary_text: Mandatory allergen declaration for 8 major allergens and their derivatives in health supplements. 'Contains: [allergen]' statement required in bold on the label even if already declared in ingredient list. Applies to: milk, eggs, fish, shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat (gluten), soy. Precautionary allergen labelling ('may contain') also standardised.
diff_text:
8 Mandatory declared allergens:
1. Milk (lactose, casein, whey derivatives)
2. Eggs (albumin, lecithin from egg)
3. Fish (fish gelatin, fish oil — species must be named)
4. Shellfish (shrimp, crab, lobster, prawn derivatives)
5. Tree nuts (almond, cashew, walnut, pistachio, hazel nut)
6. Peanuts (groundnut oil, peanut protein)
7. Wheat/Gluten (barley, rye, oats unless certified gluten-free)
8. Soy (soy lecithin, soy protein isolate)

Format: 'CONTAINS: MILK, SOY' in BOLD, font ≥ ingredient list font size
Precautionary: 'MAY CONTAIN TRACES OF NUTS' — only if genuine cross-contamination risk exists; cannot be used as substitute for proper allergen management

document_name: FSSAI Advisory: Prohibited Health Claims — Disease Treatment, Cure and Prevention Language
summary_text: FSSAI issues advisory with specific examples of prohibited claims found in e-commerce listings and label copy. Companies found using prohibited disease claims face product suspension and show-cause notice. Includes 'implied cure' claims through before/after imagery, testimonials claiming disease reversal, and algorithm-targeted marketing language.
diff_text:
Explicitly prohibited claim patterns (examples from enforcement actions):

DISEASE TREATMENT claims (prohibited):
- 'Treats diabetes / controls blood sugar in diabetics'
- 'Cures joint pain / arthritis treatment'
- 'Reverses fatty liver / treats NAFLD'
- 'Kills cancer cells / anti-tumour'

DISEASE PREVENTION claims (prohibited):
- 'Prevents heart disease / heart attack prevention'
- 'Prevents diabetes / reduces diabetes risk'
- 'Prevents cancer'
- 'Prevents Alzheimer's disease'

IMPLIED DISEASE claims (prohibited):
- 'For diabetics' (implies therapeutic use)
- Before/after imagery showing disease reversal
- Testimonials: 'Stopped my insulin' / 'Cured my arthritis'

PERMITTED structure-function claims (permitted with substantiation):
- 'Supports healthy blood sugar levels already within normal range'
- 'Supports joint flexibility and mobility'
- 'Supports liver health'
- 'Antioxidant support'
- 'Supports healthy immune function'

document_name: FSSAI Advisory on Protein Supplement Labelling — Amino Acid Profile and Protein Quality
summary_text: Following market surveillance finding adulteration in protein powders (spiking with non-protein nitrogen: creatine, taurine, glycine), FSSAI now requires protein supplements to declare: (1) complete amino acid profile per serving, (2) PDCAAS or DIAAS score, (3) source of protein (whey concentrate/isolate/hydrolysate, pea, soy, rice — percentage of each blend). False protein content claims attract prosecution under FSS Act 2006.
diff_text:
New mandatory declarations on protein supplement labels:

1. Protein per serving (g)
2. Protein per 100g
3. Source(s) of protein with percentage: e.g. 'Whey Protein Concentrate (70%), Whey Protein Isolate (30%)'
4. Complete amino acid profile per serving (Essential + Non-essential)
5. Protein quality score: PDCAAS (min acceptable) or DIAAS (preferred)

Prohibited practices:
- Nitrogen spiking (adding free amino acids/creatine/taurine solely to inflate Kjeldahl protein reading)
- Claiming 'X g protein' when true protein (by DUMAS method) is lower
- Blending plant protein with lower DIAAS without disclosure

Testing requirement: Batch-level CoA from NABL-accredited lab for protein content and amino acid profile mandatory for each production batch

document_name: FSSAI Order: Restrictions on Health Claims for Probiotic Supplements — CFU and Strain-Specific Claims
summary_text: Probiotic supplements may only claim viable cell count (CFU) if guaranteed at end of shelf life, not just at manufacture. Strain-specific health claims (e.g. 'Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG reduces diarrhoea duration') require submission of clinical substantiation dossier to FSSAI before use. Generic 'gut health' claims remain permitted as structure-function claims.
diff_text:
Probiotic-specific claim rules:

CFU CLAIMS:
- Must state CFU at end of shelf life (not manufacture date)
- Format: 'X Billion CFU at time of manufacture; Y Billion CFU at best before date'
- Storage conditions that affect CFU viability must be stated

STRAIN-SPECIFIC HEALTH CLAIMS:
- Require pre-approval — submit dossier to FSSAI SRCD
- Dossier must include: 2 RCTs in Indian or equivalent population, meta-analysis preferred
- Claim must specify strain to genus-species-strain level: e.g. L. acidophilus NCFM®

PERMITTED without pre-approval:
- 'Contains live cultures'
- 'Supports digestive health'
- 'Promotes healthy gut flora balance'

PROHIBITED:
- 'Clinically proven to treat IBS' (disease claim)
- Generic CFU claims without viability guarantee
- Using strain trade names without substantiation on file

document_name: FSSAI Guidance: Digital Labelling and QR Code Requirements for Packaged Health Supplements
summary_text: FSSAI introduces voluntary (transitioning to mandatory) QR code framework for health supplements. QR code must link to FSSAI-registered product page containing batch details, lab reports, and full ingredient information. QR content must be in English; Hindi version encouraged. Label physical information cannot be replaced by QR — QR is supplementary.
diff_text:
QR Code requirements:

Phase 1 (2024-09-01): Voluntary for all health supplements
Phase 2 (2025-04-01): Mandatory for products with >50 ingredients or complex formulations

QR must link to a page containing:
  1. Complete ingredient list (INCI names where applicable)
  2. NABL lab test Certificate of Analysis for current batch
  3. Nutritional information detailed view
  4. FSSAI product registration/approval number
  5. Manufacturer's FSMS certification status
  6. Batch-specific allergen status

QR Code specifications:
  - Minimum size: 10mm × 10mm
  - Error correction level: M (15% recovery)
  - Must be scannable by standard mobile device from 30cm
  - URL must remain active for shelf life + 2 years minimum
  - Cannot require app download to access content

document_name: FSSAI Notification: Mandatory Declaration of Added Sugars in Health Supplement Nutritional Table
summary_text: Health supplements containing added sugars (sucrose, glucose, fructose, corn syrup, honey, agave, maltodextrin used as sweetener) must declare 'Added Sugars: Xg' in the nutritional table as a sub-line under Total Sugars. Applies to gummies, chewable tablets, syrups, and flavoured powders. Zero-added-sugar claim requires '<0.5g added sugars per serving'.
diff_text:
Nutritional table format change:

Previous format (Total Carbohydrate section):
  Total Carbohydrate — Xg
    of which Sugars — Xg

New mandatory format:
  Total Carbohydrate — Xg
    of which Total Sugars — Xg
      of which Added Sugars — Xg  ← NEW mandatory line
    Dietary Fibre — Xg

Definition of 'Added Sugars' includes:
  - White sugar, raw sugar, brown sugar, icing sugar
  - Corn syrup, high-fructose corn syrup, dextrose
  - Honey, maple syrup, agave nectar
  - Maltodextrin when used as sweetener/filler
  - Fruit juice concentrate used for sweetening
  - Does NOT include: natural sugars in whole fruit, lactose in dairy

Naturally occurring sugars (intrinsic) need not be separately declared as 'Added'

Permitted 'No Added Sugar' claims: <0.5g added sugars per stated serving

document_name: FSSAI Guidance Document: Structure-Function Claim Substantiation Framework for Nutraceuticals
summary_text: First formal substantiation framework for structure-function claims. Companies must maintain a substantiation dossier for each claim made on pack. Dossier to be submitted to FSSAI on request. Permitted claim sources: EFSA approved claims, FDA authorised health claims (adapted for Indian context), ICMR position papers, or 2 peer-reviewed RCTs. Blanket disclaimer 'These statements have not been evaluated by FSSAI' is not acceptable.
diff_text:
Substantiation hierarchy (highest to lowest):

Level 1 — FSSAI pre-approved claim list (to be published by Jan 2025)
  Example: 'Calcium and Vitamin D contribute to normal bone health'
  No additional substantiation needed

Level 2 — EFSA/FDA equivalence
  Existing EFSA Scientific Opinion or FDA Authorised Health Claim
  Must submit: Original regulatory document + adaptation note for Indian context

Level 3 — ICMR/NIN position paper
  Published position paper from ICMR, NIN, or equivalent Indian body
  Must submit: Specific paper + relevant excerpt

Level 4 — Clinical evidence dossier
  Minimum: 2 independent peer-reviewed RCTs (Cochrane risk of bias low/moderate)
  Preferred: Meta-analysis or systematic review
  Population: Indian or South Asian preferred; Western data acceptable if physiological equivalence argued

Record keeping: Dossier must be retained for 5 years from claim discontinuation
Inspection: FSSAI officers may request dossier during inspection; 14-day response window

document_name: FSSAI Circular: Mandatory Warning Statements and Contraindication Disclosures on Health Supplements
summary_text: Expands mandatory warning statements for health supplements. In addition to the existing 'NOT FOR MEDICINAL USE', labels must now carry 'Consult your physician before use if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, on medication, or have a medical condition.' Iron supplements >18mg/day: additional 'Keep out of reach of children — accidental overdose can cause serious harm.' Fat-soluble vitamin supplements (A, D, E, K): 'Do not exceed stated dose — fat-soluble vitamins can accumulate.'
diff_text:
New mandatory warning statements by product category:

ALL health supplements:
  'ADVISORY: Consult your physician before use if pregnant, breastfeeding, taking medications, or have a pre-existing health condition.'
  Font: Min 1.5mm, back of pack acceptable if 'Advisory on back' appears on front

IRON supplements >18mg elemental iron/serving:
  'WARNING: Keep out of reach of children. Accidental overdose of iron is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under 6.'
  Font: Min 2mm, must appear on front of pack near dosage information

FAT-SOLUBLE VITAMINS (A, D, E, K) above 50% DV:
  'CAUTION: Do not exceed the recommended dose. Fat-soluble vitamins accumulate in the body and excessive intake may be harmful.'

HERBAL supplements:
  'This product contains [herb name]. Consult a physician if you have liver/kidney conditions.'
  (mandatory if herb has known hepatotoxicity/nephrotoxicity signal)

PRODUCTS FOR CHILDREN (if marketed for under-18):
  Must add: 'Not suitable for children under [age]. Keep out of reach of children under 3.'

document_name: Ministry of AYUSH: Regulatory Framework for Ayurvedic Health Supplements — G.S.R. 817(E)
summary_text: Ministry of AYUSH issues guidelines for Ayurvedic health supplements sold under the FSSAI framework. Products containing Ayurvedic herbs (Schedule E/K herbs) must carry 'Ayurvedic Proprietary Medicine' or 'Classical Ayurvedic Formulation' designation. Label must indicate the principal herbs in IUPAC or standard Sanskrit names. Products cannot simultaneously carry both drug license and FSSAI license.
diff_text:
Key provisions:
- Products with scheduled Ayurvedic herbs require AYUSH license (not FSSAI) if drug claims made
- FSSAI-licensed Ayurvedic supplements may only make structure-function claims
- Label must list herbs with standardised extract ratio (e.g., 'Ashwagandha root extract 5:1')
- Heavy metal testing mandatory: Pb <10ppm, Cd <0.3ppm, As <3ppm, Hg <1ppm (as per Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia)
- Products with Ashwagandha, Brahmi, Shankhpushpi, Shatavari must declare standardised constituent marker (e.g., Withanolides ≥2.5%)

document_name: AYUSH Circular: GMP Requirements Under Schedule T for Nutraceutical-Ayurvedic Hybrid Products
summary_text: AYUSH mandates that manufacturing facilities producing hybrid nutraceutical-Ayurvedic products must comply with Schedule T Good Manufacturing Practices in addition to FSSAI Schedule 4 GMP. Certificate of Analysis must include Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia reference standards. Batch manufacturing record must be maintained for minimum 5 years.
diff_text:
GMP dual compliance requirements:
- Schedule T compliance: Mandatory for all products containing ≥10% Ayurvedic herbal content by weight
- FSSAI Schedule 4: Continues to apply for food safety standards
- CoA must reference: API (Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India) monograph where applicable
- Batch records: Minimum 5 years retention
- Retained samples: Each batch — 2x commercial pack preserved for 2 years post shelf-life
- Facility audit: AYUSH licensing authority may inspect GMP compliance independent of FSSAI inspections

document_name: Ministry of AYUSH Advisory: Safety Evaluation for Botanical Extracts Exceeding Traditional Use Dosage
summary_text: AYUSH issues advisory requiring toxicological safety evaluation for any Ayurvedic or botanical ingredient when the intended daily dose exceeds the traditionally documented therapeutic dose in classical texts (Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridayam). Safety evaluation must cover acute, sub-acute, and mutagenicity studies. Applicable to high-potency extracts in capsule and tablet form.
diff_text:
Affected high-potency botanical ingredients (examples):
1. Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera): traditional dose 3-6g root powder/day; extracts delivering >600mg withanolides require safety dossier
2. Guggul (Commiphora mukul): traditional dose 500mg-2g/day; higher doses require lipid-profile monitoring data
3. Brahmi (Bacopa monnieri): doses >300mg/day extract require cholinesterase activity study
4. Senna (Cassia angustifolia): restricted — maximum 12mg sennosides/day; must not be used in products marketed for general consumption
5. Aconite (Aconitum ferox): banned unless shodhana (detoxification) purification documented and alkaloid level <0.01%

Safety dossier to be submitted to AYUSH Licensing Authority before commercial launch

document_name: AYUSH-FSSAI Joint Guidance: Traditional Use Claims vs. Health Claims — Jurisdictional Clarity
summary_text: Joint guidance from Ministry of AYUSH and FSSAI clarifies the boundary between 'traditional use claims' (permitted under AYUSH licensing without substantiation) and 'health claims' (regulated under FSSAI and requiring substantiation). Products holding FSSAI license may not use classical Ayurvedic text references as evidence for health claims — FSSAI substantiation hierarchy applies. Products holding AYUSH license may use classical text references but may not use FSSAI-style structure-function claim language.
diff_text:
Claim jurisdiction matrix:

FSSAI-licensed products:
  - 'As per Charaka Samhita...' → NOT PERMITTED as health claim support
  - Must use FSSAI substantiation hierarchy (Level 1-4)
  - 'Traditionally used in Ayurveda for...' → only permitted as HISTORICAL NOTE, not health claim
  - Example permitted: 'Ashwagandha is an adaptogenic herb traditionally used in Ayurveda. This product supports healthy stress response.' (with FSSAI Level 2-3 substantiation for the structure-function claim)

AYUSH-licensed products:
  - May reference classical texts as primary evidence
  - Cannot use FSSAI structure-function claim language if product does not hold FSSAI license
  - Drug claims prohibited in both licensing frameworks

Dual-licensed products (AYUSH + FSSAI): Not permitted — must choose one framework

document_name: Ministry of AYUSH Notification: Mandatory AYUSH Premium Mark for Quality-Certified Herbal Supplements
summary_text: Ministry of AYUSH introduces the 'AYUSH Premium Mark' — a voluntary quality certification for Ayurvedic health supplements meeting enhanced GMP, heavy metal, microbial, and pesticide residue standards. Products displaying the AYUSH Premium Mark must maintain third-party audit certification and batch-level CoA. Voluntary from January 2025; under review for mandatory status in 2026.
diff_text:
AYUSH Premium Mark requirements:

Eligibility:
- Valid AYUSH or FSSAI license
- Schedule T GMP compliance verified by NABL-accredited auditor
- Heavy metals: Meet WHO guidelines (not just API limits)
  Pb <2ppm, Cd <0.3ppm, As <1ppm, Hg <0.1ppm
- Pesticide residues: EU MRLs applied (stricter than Indian defaults)
- Microbial: Total aerobic count <10,000 CFU/g; E.coli absent/g; Salmonella absent/25g
- Authenticity: DNA barcoding for botanical identity (genus/species confirmation)

Label display:
- AYUSH Premium Mark logo (to be downloaded from AYUSH portal)
- 'Certified for Quality by Ministry of AYUSH' text alongside mark
- Certification number and expiry date on label or QR code

Renewal: Annual re-certification required

document_name: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules 2011 — Consolidated Base Regulation for Food Supplements
summary_text: The Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules 2011 establish mandatory pre-packaging declarations for all packaged food products sold in India, including health supplements and nutraceuticals. Mandates net content declaration in metric units, MRP inclusive of all taxes, manufacturer/packer name and address, month and year of manufacture/expiry, and consumer care details. Applies to all packaged commodities sold by weight, volume, or count.
diff_text:
Mandatory declarations under PC Rules 2011 (Rule 6):

1. Name and address of the manufacturer/packer/importer
2. Net quantity (weight in grams/kg for solids; volume in ml/litres for liquids; count for unit packs)
3. Month and year of manufacture (or 'Best before' date)
4. Maximum Retail Price (MRP): Rs. X.XX inclusive of all taxes
   Format: 'MRP Rs. X (Incl. of all taxes)'
5. Consumer Care details: name and address/phone number
6. Country of origin for imported goods
7. For multi-piece packs: total number of pieces + price per piece

Penalty: Fine up to Rs. 25,000 for first offence; Rs. 50,000 and imprisonment for repeat offences
Enforcement: State Weights & Measures departments; Legal Metrology officers

document_name: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Amendment Rules 2017 — E-Commerce and Online Marketplace Labelling
summary_text: Amendment extends PC Rules 2011 obligations to e-commerce platforms. Online product listings must display all mandatory label declarations (MRP, net weight, manufacturer details, expiry date) on the product detail page before purchase. E-commerce entities are jointly liable for non-compliant listings. Marketplaces must maintain seller compliance records.
diff_text:
E-commerce specific requirements (new Rule 18):

Online product listing must display:
- MRP (inclusive of taxes) prominently
- Net quantity
- Best before / expiry date
- Name and address of manufacturer/packer
- Country of origin

E-commerce platform obligations:
- Must not list products without complete mandatory declarations
- Responsible for ensuring seller-uploaded information is accurate
- Must have grievance redressal mechanism for mislabelled products
- Annual compliance report to be submitted to DPIIT

Penalty: E-commerce platforms face same penalties as manufacturers for non-compliance
Grace period: 6 months for existing listings to comply

document_name: Legal Metrology Amendment 2022 — Digital Price Display and QR Code Integration for Packaged Commodities
summary_text: Amendment permits MRP and mandatory declarations to be displayed via QR code in addition to physical label printing, subject to conditions. Physical MRP declaration remains mandatory. QR code may supplement but not replace physical declarations. Applicable to packaged commodities including health supplements, with specific size and readability requirements for digital content.
diff_text:
QR code supplementary declarations:

Permitted:
- QR code may link to a page showing all mandatory PC Rules declarations in digital format
- Useful for multi-language compliance (Hindi + regional language via QR)
- Batch-specific information (MRP changes, promotional pricing) may be updated digitally

NOT permitted:
- QR code cannot substitute for physically printed MRP, net weight, or manufacturer name
- Physical label must remain the primary compliance vehicle

QR code specifications:
- Minimum size: 10mm x 10mm (same as FSSAI Digital Labelling guidance)
- Must be scannable without app download
- Content must be in English + Hindi minimum
- URL must remain live for at least 3 years post manufacturing date

document_name: Legal Metrology Circular: Unit Sale Price Declaration Mandatory for Multi-Unit Health Supplement Packs
summary_text: Legal Metrology circular requires 'Unit Sale Price' (price per unit of measurement: per tablet, per capsule, per gram, per 100ml) to be declared on all health supplement multi-count packs of 30 units or more. The unit sale price must appear adjacent to MRP to enable consumer price comparison. Applicable to protein powders (price per 100g), multivitamins (price per tablet), and supplement liquids (price per serving).
diff_text:
Unit Sale Price declaration requirements:

Applicable to:
- Multi-count packs: ≥30 capsules/tablets/softgels
- Powders: any size pack
- Liquid supplements: any volume pack

Format:
  'MRP Rs. XXX (Incl. of all taxes)
   Unit Price: Rs. X.XX per capsule' (or per gram, per 100ml, etc.)

Placement:
- Must appear within 5mm of MRP declaration
- Same font size as MRP or larger
- Not required for samples or single-serve packs (<30 units)

Exemptions:
- Promotional combo packs with different SKUs
- Gift packs with non-standard configurations

Enforcement: State Legal Metrology officers; applicable from January 2025

document_name: FSS (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) First Amendment Regulations 2025 — S.O. 247(E)
summary_text: First Amendment to FSS Food Products Standards — updates additive limits for health supplements. Bans titanium dioxide (E171) as food colour. Revised limits for preservatives in liquid supplements. New sweetener limits for stevia in supplement gummies. Mandatory INS number declaration for all food additives.
diff_text:
Key changes:

1. Titanium dioxide (E171): BANNED as food additive in all food categories
   - Effective immediately; 6 months for label transition
   - Follows EFSA 2021 safety assessment

2. Preservative limits revised (liquid supplements):
   - Sodium benzoate: max 250 ppm (was 300)
   - Potassium sorbate: max 1000 ppm (unchanged)
   - Parabens: methylparaben max 120 ppm, propylparaben max 12 ppm

3. Artificial sweetener labelling:
   - 'CONTAINS ARTIFICIAL SWEETENER' mandatory on front panel
   - Aspartame: add 'CONTAINS PHENYLALANINE' warning

4. All additives must declare INS number alongside class name

document_name: FSS (Labelling and Display) Regulations 2020 — Version VIII Amendment (September 2025)
summary_text: Version VIII of the Labelling & Display Regulations introduces Front-of-Pack Nutrition Labelling (FOPNL) with Health Star Rating or warning symbols, mandatory added sugars declaration in nutritional tables, and QR code requirements for complex formulations. FOPNL mandatory for products exceeding threshold limits for sugar, sodium, saturated fat, or trans fat per serving.
diff_text:
Version VIII key changes:

1. FRONT-OF-PACK NUTRITION LABELLING (FOPNL):
   - Mandatory for products exceeding: Sugar >6g/serving, Sodium >600mg, Sat Fat >3g, Trans Fat >0.5g
   - Health Star Rating (0.5 to 5 stars) OR warning triangle symbols
   - Location: Principal display panel, upper right quadrant
   - Minimum size: 15% of front panel area

2. ADDED SUGARS DECLARATION:
   - Sub-line under Total Sugars: 'of which Added Sugars — Xg'
   - Definition includes corn syrup, honey, maltodextrin as sweetener
   - 'No Added Sugar': only if <0.5g per serving

3. QR CODE (Phase 2 — mandatory):
   - Required for products with >50 ingredients
   - Must link to FSSAI product page with CoA, ingredient details
   - Minimum 10mm x 10mm, scannable from 30cm

4. ALLERGEN DECLARATION UPDATE:
   - Bold font minimum same size as ingredient list
   - 'May contain' only if genuine cross-contamination risk documented

document_name: FSSAI Licensing & Registration Amendment Regulations 2026 — Perpetual Validity & New Turnover Thresholds
summary_text: Major licensing reform: (1) New turnover thresholds — Registration up to ₹1.5 Cr, State License up to ₹50 Cr, Central License above ₹50 Cr. (2) Perpetual license validity — no renewal cycles; one-time grant with perpetual validity. (3) Deemed registration for street vendors under Street Vendors Act 2014. (4) Risk-based inspection framework replacing calendar-based audits.
diff_text:
Licensing threshold changes:

REGISTRATION (previously up to ₹12 lakh):
  New threshold: up to ₹1.5 Crore annual turnover
  Validity: Perpetual (no renewal)

STATE LICENSE (previously ₹12 lakh to ₹20 Cr):
  New threshold: ₹1.5 Cr to ₹50 Crore
  Validity: Perpetual

CENTRAL LICENSE (previously above ₹20 Cr):
  New threshold: above ₹50 Crore
  Validity: Perpetual

STREET VENDORS:
  Deemed registration under FSSAI if registered under Street Vendors Act 2014
  No separate application required

INSPECTION FRAMEWORK:
  Risk-based: High-risk (annual), Medium (biennial), Low (triennial)
  Replaces calendar-based inspection schedule
  Risk categorisation based on: product type, compliance history, consumer complaints

document_name: FSSAI Order: Mandatory Testing for Ethylene Oxide Residues in Health Supplements
summary_text: FSSAI mandates ethylene oxide (EtO) residue testing for all health supplements containing plant-based ingredients. Maximum residue limit: 0.1 mg/kg. Products exceeding limit face recall and license suspension. Follows EU detections of EtO in Indian supplement exports.
diff_text:
Ethylene oxide testing requirements:

- Applicable to: All supplements with plant/herbal ingredients
- Maximum residue limit: 0.1 mg/kg (0.1 ppm)
- Testing: GC-MS method, NABL-accredited lab
- Frequency: Each batch of incoming raw material
- CoA must include EtO residue result
- Non-compliance: Product recall + show-cause for license suspension

Background: EU RASFF alerts on Indian spices/supplements; FSSAI aligning with EU MRL

document_name: FSSAI Notification: Revised Upper Safe Limits for Vitamin B6 and New Vitamin K2 Limits
summary_text: Revised upper safe limits: Vitamin B6 lowered from 25mg/day to 10mg/day (peripheral neuropathy risk). First-time limits introduced for Vitamin K2 — MK-7: 300mcg/day, MK-4: 1500mcg/day. Products with K2 must carry anticoagulant warning. Companies have 4 months to reformulate.
diff_text:
Nutrient limit changes:

Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine):
  Previous max: 25 mg/day
  New max: 10 mg/day
  Reason: Peripheral neuropathy reports at chronic >25mg/day

Vitamin K2 (MK-7 form) — NEW:
  Max: 300 mcg/day
  Warning: 'Do not take if on anticoagulant therapy (warfarin, acenocoumarol)'

Vitamin K2 (MK-4 form) — NEW:
  Max: 1500 mcg/day
  Same anticoagulant warning

Transition: 4 months from effective date for reformulation
